title: OTLP Multiplexer: schema validation and sink isolation for resilient tracing exports
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: As we onboard more third-party backends (Tempo, Jaeger, Splunk, internal long-term store) we need a single OTLP entrypoint that can safely multiplex spans to multiple sinks while enforcing per-sink schema expectations and customer isolation. Current exporters are brittle: a schema mismatch or malformed resource attribute can take down a tenant's tracing path or cause noisy errors in downstream sinks.

Goals:
- Provide a resilient OTLP multiplexer/proxy that accepts OTLP gRPC/HTTP and fans out to configured sinks.
- Enforce lightweight schema validation and normalization rules per-sink to avoid downstream failures (eg. strict span attribute types required by X backend).
- Allow per-tenant sink isolation and rate-limits so a noisy tenant doesn't impact others.
- Support dynamic sink configuration (hot reload) and signal-based failover to fallback sinks.
- Observability: add exporter-level metrics (queue depth, per-sink success/failure rates, last schema validation error) and tracing for the multiplexer itself.

Design notes:
- Proxy will run as a separate service (otlp-multiplexer) colocated with trace ingestion layer. It exposes the same OTLP endpoints and implements a configuration-driven routing table (tenant -> [sinkA, sinkB]) with per-sink validation policy.
- Validation: use JSON Schema-inspired checks for resource and span attributes plus lightweight type coercion when safe (e.g., numeric strings -> numbers when sink supports it). Failures can be either drop-with-metric, sanitize-and-forward, or fail-fast depending on sink policy.
- Delivery semantics: async fan-out with bounded per-sink queues and backpressure strategy. If a sink is unhealthy, move to retry queue and optionally send to a configured fallback sink.
- Security: respect tenant encryption/PII redaction policies. Ensure KMS keys for sinks are scoped per-tenant.

Acceptance criteria:
- OTLP multiplexer accepts gRPC/HTTP requests and fans out to at least Tempo and internal long-term store with schema validation enabled.
- Demonstrated per-tenant isolation: noisy-tenant test must not degrade other tenants' export success rates.
- Metrics emitted to prometheus: otlp_mux_incoming_rps, otlp_mux_per_sink_success_total, otlp_mux_per_sink_validation_errors_total, otlp_mux_queue_depth{sink,tenant}.
- Integration test matrix: normal export, schema-coercion, validation-drop, sink-failure -> fallback.
- Docs: runbook and config reference in Confluence plus example k8s manifests.

Rollout plan:
1) Deploy behind a feature flag for 10% of traffic internal-only.
2) Monitor per-sink error rates and queue metrics for 48h.
3) Gradually increase traffic and enable fallback policies.
4) Flip feature flag for all non-production tenants, then production after 2-week bake and SLO verification.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Additional operational surface area (new service) vs. benefit of centralized policy. Mitigation: lightweight service with clear health endpoints and autoscaling.
- Schema enforcement may drop spans; default policy is sanitize-and-forward to avoid data loss unless tenant opts into strict mode.
- Increased latency for fan-out: we will keep user-facing path async and only block on validation, not on downstream ack.

- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/OTLP+Multiplexer+Design

- Long-term store schema: https://docs.redwood.ai/long-term-trace-schema
comments: 2025-02-16 - Triage: scoped to OTLP gRPC/HTTP + Tempo/internal LTS for MVP. P0 behavior: sanitize-and-forward by default. Asha: assigned to Miguel for implementation.
2025-02-20 - Design review meeting: PMs requested per-tenant TTL on validation errors; added config option 'validation_error_ttl' to avoid repeated noisy logs.

2025-02-25 - Implementation update: basic gRPC ingress and fan-out implemented. Added per-sink bounded queue and prometheus metrics. Unit tests for coercion rules added. Branch: feature/otlp-mux-basic.

2025-02-28 - Code review comments (from Lina): prefer explicit schema versions per sink; add compatibility check in hot-reload. Miguel responded: added version check and fallback to 'legacy' normalization rules.
2025-03-02 - QA: integration test failures observed when Tempo rejects spans with empty 'service.name' attribute. Decided to coerce from resource.service.name when present. Adding e2e test case.
2025-03-03 - Deployment plan updated: initial rollout only for internal tenants and non-prod; added alert otlp_mux_per_sink_validation_errors_total > 10/min for 5m to trigger rollback if necessary.
